text.p: LME nickel steamed higher on Monday afternoon on mainly chart buying and short-covering, but the other metals held to narrow ranges.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index was 1.78 points higher at 242.06.

Three months nickel peaked at $6,945 per tonne, a gain of $340 or five percent on Friday's afternoon kerb close, after it earlier broke above a key trendline, analysts said. Nickel had become oversold recently as funds went short, bottoming at $6,365 on December 30. Last year, prices hit a high of $8,850 in February. By the end of the kerb, profit-taking had taken the froth off the market to end at $6,860, up $255.
The other metals marked time, holding in tight price bands.
Copper finished $2 higher at $2,195, after turning back from resistance at $2,200 ahead of stocks data on Tuesday, which some traders are expecting to show an increase.

Aluminium finished the day at $1,552, down $2. Analysts say the market needs to consolidate further before tackling solid resistance at $1,570, where producer selling is expected to make progress difficult. Support was pegged at $1,530.
Zinc ended at $1,064, up $2 and lead closed $4 weaker at $696.
Tin finished the kerb unchanged at $5,760 while aluminium alloy was indicated at $1,430/35, little changed from Friday's $1,430/33.

CBOT wheat futures were sharply higher at midsession in response to weather-related concerns about the U.S. winter wheat crop, traders said. At 1048 CST, CBOT wheat was up six to eight cents per bushel, with March up eight at $3.92. May wheat was up 6-1/2 cents per bushel at $3.70-1/2.

NYMEX crude was catapulted more than 80 cents a barrel Monday afternoon by a heating oil rally after a cold spell was forecasted for the U.S. Northeast. "Crude was already in a bullish trend, but it would not have been this strong without heating oil," said a New York crude dealer. At 1419 EST, February crude was up 88 cents at $26.47 a barrel, the session high. February heating oil was up 2.96 cents at 74.25 cents a gallon, below the session high of 74.50. Spot crude's technical resistance was pegged at $26.80, the post-Gulf War high made December 19.

CSCE world sugar prices retreated toward unchanged at midsession, after an early round of fund buying ran into stiff resistance, dealers said. Sporadic selling by producers and the trade was noted at the highs, traders said, while good buying of the March-May switch provided some support. At 1133 EST, March futures were down 0.01 cent per lb, at 11.07 cents, having traded from 11.00 to 11.11. Second-position May was up 0.02 cent, while the outer months were down 0.01 to up 0.03.

New York precious metals futures remained sharply lower midday Monday, after gold fell to new three year lows during the morning. "We saw some trade selling after the opening on good volume, but the action has quieted down now and silver is holding up pretty well," one floor trader said. COMEX February gold was down $3.50 an ounce at $358.50 midday, after seeing a fresh life-of-contract low at $358.00. Spot gold in the bullion market was quoted $357.30/357.80, after gold fixed at $358.50 an ounce in London Monday afternoon, the lowest since October 7, 1993.
